# The machine-wide stage budget: at most max_concurrent stage commands run at once
# across EVERY breeze daemon on this box, and a stage arriving when the budget is
# full WAITS rather than failing. The slots are flock'd files in a shared directory,
# so a daemon killed mid-run cannot leak one.
env XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$WORK/cfg
env BREEZE_DIR=$WORK/state
mkdir $WORK/cfg/breeze

exec breeze register identity ci
cp stdout ci.token
exec breeze apply -f pipeline.hcl --as ci --token-file ci.token

# The budget is legible: a shared limit nobody can inspect turns "why is my build
# not starting" into a question with no answer.
exec breeze status
stdout 'machine-wide stage budget: 1 concurrent'

# Occupy the only slot, then start a second stage. It queues rather than running.
exec sh -c 'breeze start stage svc slow abc --as ci --token-file ci.token >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 1'
exec sh -c 'breeze start stage svc quick abc --as ci --token-file ci.token >$WORK/quick.out 2>&1 & sleep 1'

exec breeze status stage svc quick abc
stdout 'quick: queued'

# And the occupancy names WHICH REPO is holding the machine, which is the first
# thing anyone asks when their build is behind something.
exec breeze status
stdout 'machine-wide stage budget: 1 concurrent, 1 in use'
stdout 'svc/slow'

# A queued stage counts against the restart guard: it has no process, but it does
# have a goroutine holding its place, and a re-exec destroys that.
! exec breeze restart daemon
stderr 'queued for a machine slot'

# Once the slot frees, the queued stage runs — it waited, it did not fail.
exec sh -c 'sleep 5; cat $WORK/quick.out'
stdout 'succeeded'

exec breeze stop

-- pipeline.hcl --
pipeline "svc" {
  stage "slow" {
    type    = "command"
    timeout = "60s"
    command = ["/bin/sleep", "4"]
  }
  stage "quick" {
    type    = "command"
    needs   = []
    timeout = "60s"
    command = ["/bin/true"]
  }
}

-- cfg/breeze/defaults.hcl --
queue {
  max_concurrent = 1
  wait_timeout   = "60s"
}
